title: O God of Our Salvation
description: O God of Our Salvation in Tonic Solfa to GREENLAND, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), and this page sets them to GREENLAND; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God of our sal-va-tion, Who in Thy glo-rious might, Didst speak, and all cre-a-tion A-rose from brood-ing night; And cha-os, and con-fu-sion, To form and or-der sped, While lo! in rich pro-fu-sion The earth its beau-ty spread.

lines: Thy word hath still its power,
Speak as of old, and banish

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to GREENLAND by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
